newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST- Semiconductor earnings seen dismal in Q3.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST- Semiconductor earnings seen dismal in Q3.

text.p: Despite reports of rising demand for computer chips recently, earnings for most semiconductors makers in the calendar third quarter are expected to be dismal, with the exception of Intel Corp and a few others.

"The third quarter is too soon. You're going to have to wait until the fourth quarter" for increased chip demand to show up in revenues and earnings, said Dan Niles of Robertson, Stephens & Co. "The third quarter is going to be horrendous for most companies."
However, Niles and other analysts expect sequential and year-over-year gains in the fourth quarter.

"This is probably the bottom quarter for earnings, and then we would envision them to show sequential growth in the fourth quarter," said PaineWebber's John Lazlo. "The third quarter will be flat to down" for most companies.
The exceptions are Intel Corp, Adaptec Inc, S3 Inc, Microchip Technology Corp and Atmel Corp, which all should show higher profits, Laslo said.
Other analysts also named Intel, Adaptec and S3 as likely to show third-quarter earnings gains.
Atmel already reported third-quarter earnings rose to $0.53 a share from $0.31 in the same period last year.
Those companies should benefit from their heavy sales to personal computer makers.

PC makers have recently boosted their production in time for the big selling seasons of fall and the December holidays. To do so, they've been buying up microprocessors and PC graphics chips and audio chips at an accelerated pace.
Intel tipped off industry watchers to the surge in PC chip sales a few weeks ago with a rare announcement revising its outlook to expect sales gains between the second and third quarters.
Wall Street's mean estimate on Intel's third-quarter earnings is $1.25 a share, according to First Call. That compares with $1.02 EPS in last year's third quarter.
The mean estimate on S3 is $0.22 a share, according to First Call, compared with $0.20 EPS in the year-ago quarter.
For Adaptec's second quarter ending September, the mean estimate is $0.76 a share, according to First Call, up from $0.61 in the year-ago quarter.
For Microchip Technology, the mean estimate is $0.36 a share for its second quarter ending in September, according to First Call, versus $0.35 a year ago.

"The only improvement in third-quarter earnings will come from PC-related companies, and maybe some differentiated companies" -- those whose products are proprietary or not made by anyone else -- said Bear Stearns analyst Nimal Vallipuram.
"What happened in September is not going to help them, it is too late," he said. Texas Instruments Inc is the only major memory chip maker whose reporting quarters follow the calendar year.
Wall Street's mean estimate on Texas Instruments' third quarter is $0.20 a share, according to First Call. That would mark a sharp drop from the $1.48 a share it earned in the year-ago third quarter.
However, if memory prices increase, as they have in recent weeks, that could boost fourth-quarter earnings, analysts said.
